goal: Integrate the frozen dual-XGMII HFT baseline with the frozen RMIC M5.4 transactional core without modifying either upstream, while closing TAIFEX futures accounting, execution idempotency, safety-policy, timing, and end-to-end validation gaps.
handoff: I5 full dual-XGMII integration source and local verification flows are prepared. The integration-owned hierarchy preserves frozen network/TCP/session/replay ownership, routes both R01 producers through the closed I4 risk boundary, aligns committed R02/R32 futures metadata by msg_type+order_id+report_seq, and queues committed execution pulses before the serialized shared risk core. Exact-head governance and unit regressions pass; the remaining I5 gates require local compilation/simulation and U50 implementation against the pinned private upstreams.
next_action: Run the packaged I5 dual-XGMII functional XSim first. After its ZIP is reviewed, run the real-XPM U50 dual-XGMII OOC implementation; use those results to fix/close I5 functional and physical integration before measuring a new latency baseline.

tasks.acceptance: Self-checking simulation proves market event→strategy→risk→R01, reject suppression, committed fill→state reconciliation, and session/replay behavior without modifying pinned upstreams.

tasks.acceptance: Reproducible Vivado evidence reports timing/resources/critical path/DRC/power for the combined integration top; any latency measurement uses explicitly documented boundaries.

milestones.summary: HFT and RMIC upstreams pinned as read-only submodules at frozen pre-integration baselines.
Order field mapping and fail-closed policy shell established with integration-level reject namespace.
Futures accounting v1 separates long/short and OPEN/CLOSE semantics using a host-configured margin-per-contract research model; not a TAIFEX SPAN claim.
Integration-owned R02/R32 fixed-offset tap captures PositionEffect and before_qty fields missing from the frozen HFT decoder; mutation authority remains external committed-report ownership.
LOB-inspired phase governance adopted: canonical project state, append-only decisions, living ExecPlan, one phase branch/PR, evidence-layer boundaries and mechanical governance CI.
Multi-account/product futures state manager regression closed key isolation, OPEN/CLOSE long/short semantics, margin reject, fail-closed ownership, configuration priority and reset recovery.
A 96-bit futures order context keyed by order_id reuses the frozen RMIC AMU contract without reusing stock-like account accounting.
Committed R02/R32 and R03 reconciliation passes partial/final fill, terminal release, cancel, reduce, replay/stale fail-closed and release-once scenarios.
Real-AMU I2 U50 OOC closes at 156.25 MHz after structural state/margin pipelining: routed WNS +1.078 ns, TNS 0, 3396 LUT, 2383 FF, 19 RAMB36 + 1 RAMB18, 10 DSP and zero routing errors.

Atomic CL2EX admission regression proves policy/accounting no-mutation, successful reserve+insert, duplicate/full rollback, stable result backpressure and no leaked reservation after recoverable store failure; its AMU INSERT found-bit assumption was later corrected in I4.
Fault injection proves an admission rollback failure can never accept an order and is escalated to an explicit recovery-required system failure.
Frozen-HFT order-gate regression closes exact account/product mapping, Side translation, mapping/policy fail-closed behavior, normalized context correctness and byte-identical accepted payload.

Real-AMU I3 atomic CL2EX U50 OOC physically closes at 156.25 MHz: synth WNS +3.023 ns, routed WNS +1.583 ns, TNS 0, 2392 LUT, 2693 FF, 11 RAMB36 + 1 RAMB18, 10 DSP and zero routing errors; later I4 evidence narrows the original real-AMU functional-contract claim.

Shared-core regression proves one futures-state/AMU owner across CL admission and committed execution, including OPEN-to-fill-to-CLOSE closed loop and execution priority under simultaneous acquisition.
Focused R01-boundary regression proves ordinary and prebuild order sources both traverse risk, prebuild retains priority, and kill-switch rejection cannot reach the encoder contract.

First real pinned-AMU/frozen-encoder parity run exposed that successful new INSERT reports found=0; admission, CI stub and lifecycle tests were corrected to the frozen AMU contract and the full exact-head regression stack passed again.
Corrected pinned frozen-encoder XSim proves exact 80-byte R01 parity for legacy and prebuild accepted orders and zero integrated R01 bytes for a kill-switch reject.

Real-XPM I4 risk-to-frozen-R01 U50 OOC closes at 156.25 MHz: synth WNS +2.310 ns, routed WNS +0.827 ns, TNS 0, 5596 LUT, 4454 FF, 19 RAMB36 + 1 RAMB18, 10 DSP, zero routing errors; the worst path remains inside the frozen AMU.
I5 unit regressions close keyed live/replay futures metadata alignment and fail-closed mismatch handling before committed execution reaches the shared risk core.

Committed execution pulses are buffered before the serialized shared risk core; FIFO overflow is sticky and escalates the full app into recovery-required rather than silently dropping an exchange event.

Integration-owned risk-aware round-chip, trading-port XGMII and dual-XGMII derivatives plus frozen-regression XSim and real-XPM OOC runners are prepared; local private-upstream Vivado evidence remains pending.
